title: Sales Enablement Playbook — Positioning, Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the core positioning, messaging, competitive brief template, pitch-deck guidance, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ for Redwood Inference. It is intended for AEs, SDRs, SEs, and GTM enablement teams to accelerate prospect conversations and RFP responses while keeping technical accuracy and compliance alignment.

Target audiences
- Mid-market and enterprise product/ML/Platform teams evaluating inference providers
- Engineering and SRE stakeholders responsible for latency, cost, and reliability
- Security, legal, and compliance reviewers for procurement

1) Positioning & One-liners
- Elevator (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, and cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so engineering teams can ship LLM features without building and operating custom serving stacks.
- For technical buyers: "Ship production-grade LLM features with consistent latency and unit economics across cloud-hosted, dedicated, and private environments."
- For economic buyers: "Reduce per-token inference cost through workload-aware batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations while meeting latency SLOs."

2) Core Messaging Pillars (use in all collateral)
- Production-grade performance: SLA-backed latency targets, autoscaling reserved capacity, and optimized GPU runtimes.
- Unified API & operations: One API and set of operational controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Cost control & transparency: Token-level cost breakdowns, batching/quantization guidance, and recommended configs that map to unit economics.
- Security & compliance: Support for VPC/private deployments, KMS/HSM key control, audit logs, and evidence for common frameworks (SOC2/ISO/GDPR).
- Developer experience: Quickstarts, SDKs, and eval tooling to catch quality regressions before rollout.

3) Competitive Brief Template (one-page, keep to bullets)
- Competitor: <Name>
- Why it matters: Short note on competitor positioning and product strengths.
- Typical customer fit: Which buyer profiles pick them (e.g., bespoke infra teams, pure-play hosted API buyers).
- Key differentiators vs Redwood:
  - Redwood advantage 1 (runtime optimizations / unified runtimes)
  - Redwood advantage 2 (private deployment + managed control plane)
  - Redwood advantage 3 (cost controls and transparent token-level billing)
- Weaknesses to call out tactfully:
  - e.g. limited observability, fewer deployment modes, hidden egress/network costs
- Sales talking points (2–3 bullets): Tailored rebuttals and demo hooks

Competitive quick matrix (2x3)
| Capability                     | Redwood Inference | Competitor A | Competitor B |
|-------------------------------|-------------------|--------------|--------------|
| Deployment modes (Hosted/Ded) | Hosted/Ded/Private| Hosted/Ded   | Hosted only  |
| Observability & cost tooling  | Full stack        | Basic        | Advanced     |
| Private deployment support    | Yes (VPC+on-prem)  | Limited      | No           |

4) Pitch Deck: recommended structure (10–14 slides)
1. Title & Hook — One-line customer-focused problem statement and outcome
2. Why now — market signals (open models, growth in LLM features)
3. Customer problem & cost/latency pain (examples)
4. Redwood overview — product modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
5. Technical differentiators — serving runtime, smart routing, caching
6. Observability & ops — Console, token-level billing, rollouts
7. Performance & cost benchmarks — representative numbers vs OSS baseline (example: 2–4x lower per-token cost at 99th-pct latency target)
8. Security & compliance — VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2/ISO readiness
9. Pricing overview & deployment options (sample tiers)
10. Case study — customer X: problem, solution, results
11. Implementation plan — timeline (P0–P2), owners, success metrics
12. Pricing/add-ons & next steps
13. Appendix — architecture diagram, benchmarks, eval examples

Pitch deck guidance: always include a short implementation timeline and a success metrics slide tailored to the prospect (e.g., target p99 latency, target per-request cost, uptime). For technical decision-makers include an architecture diagram showing KV cache, batching, and smart routing.

5) Pricing guidance (playbook for initial conversations)
- High level pricing tiers (examples for conversation only — final pricing via quoting tool):
  - Hosted (pay-as-you-go): base token rate + per-embedding rate. Typical entry path for PLG customers.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed throughput with burst options (recommended for 5M+ tokens/day or predictability needs).
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): platform fee + managed service or perpetual license for on-prem builds; additional support tiers possible.
- Example anchor numbers (illustrative):
  - Hosted: $0.003 / 1k prompt tokens, $0.001 / 1k generated tokens, $0.02 / embedding (small-model) — used for conversation only, refer to pricing tool for official numbers.
  - Dedicated: Monthly commit starting at $25k/month for small GPU pool; custom sizing based on throughput profile.
  - Private: Platform fee $50k–$150k+ depending on scope, plus per-node licensing/support.
- Discounts & negotiation rules:
  - Standard volume discounts apply for annual commitments; sales ops must sign off on any deviations from the published discount bands.
  - Do not promise SLAs beyond what finance/operations has approved for Dedicated/Private without involving account exec and legal.

6) Case Studies (concise, repeatable format)
- Format: One-paragraph problem, solution, and measured results (numbers where possible).
- Example 1: FinTech Search Relevance
  - Customer: Mid-market FinTech (anonymized)
  - Problem: High latency and cost on user-facing search and question-answering features causing engagement drop-offs.
  - Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated, enabled KV caching and model quantization profile, and tuned batching for peak times.
  - Results: 45% reduction in per-query cost, 2x improvement in p95 latency; 20% increase in task completion rate.
- Example 2: Enterprise Virtual Assistant
  - Customer: Large enterprise with strict data residency and compliance needs
  - Problem: Needed on-prem inference + auditability and role-based access controls
  - Solution: Private deployment with KMS integration and extended audit logging; Redwood Console used for traceability.
  - Results: Successful security review, 0 data exfiltration events, and 3-week pilot to production timeline.

7) Security FAQ for Prospects (top questions & short, accurate answers)
Q: Can Redwood run in our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. We support VPC-hosted private deployments and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. We offer a managed control plane or a fully customer-managed installation depending on the engagement.

Q: How are encryption keys managed?
A: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSMs). For private deployments, keys can be customer-controlled and never leave the customer's environment.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and artifact retention for compliance?
A: Yes. The Redwood Console stores request/response metadata, model versioning records, rollout logs, and operator actions. Retention policies are configurable per-customer with export options for SIEM.

Q: What certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II readiness and is progressing through ISO 27001 assessments; specific evidence packages are available for enterprise prospects under an NDA.

Q: How do you prevent data leakage or model hallucination that could affect PII?
A: We recommend prompt redaction/PII scrubbing in the preprocessing layer, tokenization checks, and model-level safety evals. For sensitive workloads, run inference in Private mode where data never leaves the customer's network.

Q: How do you handle vulnerability disclosures and incident response?
A: Security incidents are handled according to our incident response runbook; we provide timely notifications to affected customers, forensic artifacts, and post-incident reports. The security team coordinates with customer contacts during escalations.

8) Sales playbook: discovery checklist and demo hooks
- Discovery checklist (example questions):
  - What is your expected QPS and peak traffic pattern?
  - What are your p50/p95/p99 latency targets for the feature?
  - Do you have compliance/regulatory constraints (e.g., data residency, retention)?
  - What is the current per-transaction cost and desired cost target?
  - Are you open to Dedicated or Private deployments, or must it remain hosted?
- Demo hooks to use based on discovery:
  - High latency pain: demo p95/p99 latency and autoscaling behavior from Dedicated cluster
  - Cost pain: show token-level cost breakdown and how batching/caching affects unit economics
  - Security/regulatory: provide architecture that isolates data; walk through KMS integration and audit logs

10) Implementation & next steps (for AE to customize per prospect)
1. Confirm deployment preference and required certifications (week 0)
2. Share baseline benchmark and cost model for prospect workload (week 1)
3. Run a short pilot (2–4 weeks) with targeted success metrics (latency, cost per request, functional accuracy)
4. Post-pilot review and production rollout plan (2–6 weeks depending on scope)
